ops.html:
• Never add or modify any code related to CODEX_​SANDBOX_​NETWORK_​DISABLED_​ENV_VAR or CODEX_​SANDBOX_​ENV_VAR.
    • You operate in a sandbox where CODEX_​SANDBOX_​NETWORK_​DISABLED=1 will be set whenever you use the shell tool. Any existing code that uses CODEX_​SANDBOX_​NETWORK_​DISABLED_​ENV_VAR was authored with this fact in mind. It is often used to early exit out of tests that the author knew you would not be able to run given your sandbox limitations.
    • Similarly, when you spawn a process using Seatbelt (/usr/​bin/​sandbox-exec), CODEX_​SANDBOX=​seatbelt will be set on the child process. Integration tests that want to run Seatbelt themselves cannot be run under Seatbelt, so checks for CODEX_​SANDBOX=​seatbelt are also often used to early exit out of tests, as appropriate.
ops.src:
- Never add or modify any code related to `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED_ENV_VAR` or `CODEX_SANDBOX_ENV_VAR`.

Any existing code that uses `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED_ENV_VAR` was authored with this fact in mind. It is often used to early exit out of tests that the author knew you would not be able to run given your sandbox limitations.

Integration tests that want to run Seatbelt themselves cannot be run under Seatbelt, so checks for `CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt` are also often used to early exit out of tests, as appropriate.

ops.html:
• When you cannot make that API change and still need a small positional-literal callsite in Rust, follow the argument_​comment_lint convention:
    • Use an exact /*param_name*/ comment before opaque literal arguments such as None, booleans, and numeric literals when passing them by position.
    • A method's sole non-self argument is exempt when the method and parameter names match, such as .enabled(false) for fn enabled(&self, enabled: bool).
    • Do not add these comments for string or char literals unless the comment adds real clarity; those literals are intentionally exempt from the lint.
    • The parameter name in the comment must exactly match the callee signature.
    • You can run just argument-​comment-lint to run the lint check locally. This is powered by Bazel, so running it the first time can be slow if Bazel is not warmed up, though incremental invocations should take <15s. Most of the time, it is best to update the PR and let CI take responsibility for checking this (or run it asynchronously in the background after submitting the PR). Note CI checks all three platforms, which the local run does not.

ops.html:
• Discourage both #[async_trait] and #[allow(async_​fn_​in_​trait)] in Rust traits.
    • Prefer native RPITIT trait methods with explicit Send bounds on the returned future, as in 3c7f013f9735 / #16630.
    • Preferred trait shape: fn foo(&self, ...) -> impl std::​future::​Future<Output = T> + Send;
    • Implementations may still use async fn foo(&self, ...) -> T when they satisfy that contract.
    • Do not use #[allow(async_​fn_​in_​trait)] as a shortcut around spelling the future contract explicitly.
ops.src:
- Discourage both `#[async_trait]` and `#[allow(async_fn_in_trait)]` in Rust traits.
  - Prefer native RPITIT trait methods with explicit `Send` bounds on the returned future, as in `3c7f013f9735` / `#16630`.
  - Preferred trait shape:
    `fn foo(&self, ...) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = T> + Send;`
  - Implementations may still use `async fn foo(&self, ...) -> T` when they satisfy that contract.
  - Do not use `#[allow(async_fn_in_trait)]` as a shortcut around spelling the future contract explicitly.

ops.html:
• Avoid large modules:
    • Prefer adding new modules instead of growing existing ones.
    • Target Rust modules under 500 LoC, excluding tests.
    • If a file exceeds roughly 800 LoC, add new functionality in a new module instead of extending the existing file unless there is a strong documented reason not to.
    • This rule applies especially to high-touch files that already attract unrelated changes, such as codex-​rs/​tui/​src/​app.rs, codex-​rs/​tui/​src/​bottom_​pane/​chat_​composer.rs, codex-​rs/​tui/​src/​bottom_​pane/​footer.rs, codex-​rs/​tui/​src/​chatwidget.rs, codex-​rs/​tui/​src/​bottom_​pane/​mod.rs, and similarly central orchestration modules.
    • When extracting code from a large module, move the related tests and module/type docs toward the new implementation so the invariants stay close to the code that owns them.
    • Avoid adding new standalone methods to codex-​rs/​tui/​src/​chatwidget.rs unless the change is trivial; prefer new modules/files and keep chatwidget.rs focused on orchestration.
ops.src:

ops.html: Over time, the codex-core crate (defined in codex-rs/core/) has become bloated because it is the largest crate, so it is often easier to add something new to codex-core rather than refactor out the library code you need so your new code neither takes a dependency on, nor contributes to the size of, codex-core.

ops.html: Particularly when introducing a new concept/​feature/API, before adding to codex-core, consider whether:

ops.html: TUI code conventions

ops.html:
• Use concise styling helpers from ratatui’s Stylize trait.
    • Basic spans: use "text".into()
    • Styled spans: use "text".red(), "text".green(), "text".magenta(), "text".dim(), etc.
    • Prefer these over constructing styles with Span::styled and Style directly.
    • Example: patch summary file lines
      • Desired: vec![" └ ".into(), "M".red(), " ".dim(), "tui/​src/​app.rs".dim()]
ops.src:
- Use concise styling helpers from ratatui’s Stylize trait.
  - Basic spans: use "text".into()
  - Styled spans: use "text".red(), "text".green(), "text".magenta(), "text".dim(), etc.
  - Prefer these over constructing styles with `Span::styled` and `Style` directly.
  - Example: patch summary file lines
    - Desired: vec!["  └ ".into(), "M".red(), " ".dim(), "tui/src/app.rs".dim()]

ops.html: TUI Styling (ratatui)
ops.src: ### TUI Styling (ratatui)

ops.html: • Prefer Stylize helpers: use "text".dim(), .bold(), .cyan(), .italic(), .underlined() instead of manual Style where possible.

ops.html: • Prefer simple conversions: use "text".into() for spans and vec![…].into() for lines; when inference is ambiguous (e.g., Paragraph::new/​Cell::from), use Line::from(spans) or Span::from(text).
ops.src: - Prefer simple conversions: use "text".into() for spans and vec![…].into() for lines; when inference is ambiguous (e.g., Paragraph::new/Cell::from), use Line::from(spans) or Span::from(text).

ops.src: - Computed styles: if the Style is computed at runtime, using `Span::styled` is OK (`Span::from(text).set_style(style)` is also acceptable).

ops.html: • Avoid hardcoded white: do not use .white(); prefer the default foreground (no color).

ops.html: • Chaining: combine helpers by chaining for readability (e.g., url.cyan().underlined()).

ops.html: • Building lines: use vec![…].into() to construct a Line when the target type is obvious and no extra type annotations are needed; otherwise use Line::from(vec![…]).

ops.html: Spawning workspace binaries in tests (Cargo vs Bazel)
ops.src: ### Spawning workspace binaries in tests (Cargo vs Bazel)

ops.html:
• Prefer codex_​utils_​cargo_​bin::​cargo_​bin("...") over assert_​cmd::​Command::​cargo_​bin(...) or escargot when tests need to spawn first-party binaries.
    • Under Bazel, binaries and resources may live under runfiles; use codex_​utils_​cargo_​bin::​cargo_bin to resolve absolute paths that remain stable after chdir.
ops.src:
- Prefer `codex_utils_cargo_bin::cargo_bin("...")` over `assert_cmd::Command::cargo_bin(...)` or `escargot` when tests need to spawn first-party binaries.
  - Under Bazel, binaries and resources may live under runfiles; use `codex_utils_cargo_bin::cargo_bin` to resolve absolute paths that remain stable after `chdir`.

ops.html: • When locating fixture files or test resources under Bazel, avoid env!("CARGO_​MANIFEST_​DIR"). Prefer codex_​utils_​cargo_​bin::​find_​resource! so paths resolve correctly under both Cargo and Bazel runfiles.
ops.src: - When locating fixture files or test resources under Bazel, avoid `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`. Prefer `codex_utils_cargo_bin::find_resource!` so paths resolve correctly under both Cargo and Bazel runfiles.

ops.html: Integration tests
ops.src: ### Integration tests

ops.html: codex_core integration testing
ops.src: #### codex_core integration testing

ops.html: • Prefer the utilities in core_​test_​support::​responses when writing end-to-end Codex tests.
ops.src: - Prefer the utilities in `core_test_support::responses` when writing end-to-end Codex tests.

ops.html: • Use TestCodexBuilder::​build_​with_​auto_​env() by default to ensure that new tests work with foreign app/exec OSes. See $remote-tests for details.
ops.src:
- Use `TestCodexBuilder::build_with_auto_env()` by default to ensure that new tests work with

ops.html: • All mount_sse* helpers return a ResponseMock; hold onto it so you can assert against outbound /responses POST bodies.
ops.src: - All `mount_sse*` helpers return a `ResponseMock`; hold onto it so you can assert against outbound `/responses` POST bodies.

ops.html: • Use ResponseMock::​single_​request() when a test should only issue one POST, or ResponseMock::​requests() to inspect every captured ResponsesRequest.
ops.src: - Use `ResponseMock::single_request()` when a test should only issue one POST, or `ResponseMock::requests()` to inspect every captured `ResponsesRequest`.

ops.html: • ResponsesRequest exposes helpers (body_json, input, function_​call_​output, custom_​tool_​call_​output, call_output, header, path, query_param) so assertions can target structured payloads instead of manual JSON digging.
ops.src: - `ResponsesRequest` exposes helpers (`body_json`, `input`, `function_call_output`, `custom_tool_call_output`, `call_output`, `header`, `path`, `query_param`) so assertions can target structured payloads instead of manual JSON digging.

ops.html: • Build SSE payloads with the provided ev_* constructors and the sse(...).
ops.src: - Build SSE payloads with the provided `ev_*` constructors and the `sse(...)`.

ops.html: • Prefer wait_for_event over wait_​for_​event_​with_​timeout.
ops.src: - Prefer `wait_for_event` over `wait_for_event_with_timeout`.

ops.html: • Prefer mount_sse_once over mount_​sse_​once_​match or mount_sse_sequence
ops.src: - Prefer `mount_sse_once` over `mount_sse_once_match` or `mount_sse_sequence`

ops.html:
• Typical pattern:

    let mock = responses::mount_sse_once(&server, responses::sse(vec![
    responses::ev_response_created("resp-1"),
    responses::ev_function_call(call_id, "shell", &serde_json::to_string(&args)?),
    responses::ev_completed("resp-1"),
])).await;

codex.submit(Op::UserTurn { ... }).await?;

// Assert request body if needed.
let request = mock.single_request();
// assert using request.function_call_output(call_id) or request.json_body() or other helpers.

ops.html: App-server API Development Best Practices
ops.src: ## App-server API Development Best Practices

ops.html: These guidelines apply to app-server protocol work in codex-rs, especially:
ops.src: These guidelines apply to app-server protocol work in `codex-rs`, especially:

ops.html: • app-​server-​protocol/​src/​protocol/​common.rs
ops.src: - `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`

ops.html: • app-​server-​protocol/​src/​protocol/​v2.rs
ops.src: - `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2.rs`

ops.html: Core Rules
ops.src: ### Core Rules

ops.html: • All active API development should happen in app-server v2. Do not add new API surface area to v1.
ops.src: - All active API development should happen in app-server v2. Do not add new API surface area to v1.

ops.html: • Follow payload naming consistently: *Params for request payloads, *Response for responses, and *Notification for notifications.
ops.src:
- Follow payload naming consistently:
  `*Params` for request payloads, `*Response` for responses, and `*Notification` for notifications.

ops.html: • Expose RPC methods as <resource>/<method> and keep <resource> singular (for example, thread/read, app/list).
ops.src: - Expose RPC methods as `<resource>/<method>` and keep `<resource>` singular (for example, `thread/read`, `app/list`).

ops.html: • Always expose fields as camelCase on the wire with #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] unless a tagged union or explicit compatibility requirement needs a targeted rename.
ops.src: - Always expose fields as camelCase on the wire with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` unless a tagged union or explicit compatibility requirement needs a targeted rename.

ops.html: • Always expose string enum values as camelCase on the wire with matching serde and TS rename_all = "camelCase" annotations unless an explicit compatibility requirement needs targeted renames.
ops.src: - Always expose string enum values as camelCase on the wire with matching serde and TS `rename_all = "camelCase"` annotations unless an explicit compatibility requirement needs targeted renames.

ops.html: • Exception: config RPC payloads are expected to use snake_case to mirror config.toml keys (see the config read/write/list APIs in app-​server-​protocol/​src/​protocol/​v2.rs).
ops.src: - Exception: config RPC payloads are expected to use snake_case to mirror config.toml keys (see the config read/write/list APIs in `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2.rs`).

ops.html: • Always set #[ts(export_to = "v2/")] on v2 request/​response/​notification types so generated TypeScript lands in the correct namespace.
ops.src: - Always set `#[ts(export_to = "v2/")]` on v2 request/response/notification types so generated TypeScript lands in the correct namespace.

ops.html: • Never use #[serde(skip_​serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] for v2 API payload fields. Exception: client->server requests that intentionally have no params may use: params: #[ts(type = "undefined")] #[serde(skip_​serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] Option<()>.
ops.src:
- Never use `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` for v2 API payload fields.
  Exception: client->server requests that intentionally have no params may use:
  `params: #[ts(type = "undefined")] #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] Option<()>`.

ops.html: • Keep Rust and TS wire renames aligned. If a field or variant uses #[serde(rename = "...")], add matching #[ts(rename = "...")].
ops.src: - Keep Rust and TS wire renames aligned. If a field or variant uses `#[serde(rename = "...")]`, add matching `#[ts(rename = "...")]`.

ops.html: • For discriminated unions, use explicit tagging in both serializers: #[serde(tag = "type", ...)] and #[ts(tag = "type", ...)].
ops.src:
- For discriminated unions, use explicit tagging in both serializers:
  `#[serde(tag = "type", ...)]` and `#[ts(tag = "type", ...)]`.

ops.html: • Prefer plain String IDs at the API boundary (do UUID parsing/conversion internally if needed).
ops.src: - Prefer plain `String` IDs at the API boundary (do UUID parsing/conversion internally if needed).

ops.html: • Timestamps should be integer Unix seconds (i64) and named *_at (for example, created_at, updated_at, resets_at).
ops.src: - Timestamps should be integer Unix seconds (`i64`) and named `*_at` (for example, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `resets_at`).

ops.html: • For experimental API surface area: use #[experimental("method/​or/​field")], derive ExperimentalApi when field-level gating is needed, and use inspect_params: true in common.rs when only some fields of a method are experimental.
ops.src:
- For experimental API surface area:
  use `#[experimental("method/or/field")]`, derive `ExperimentalApi` when field-level gating is needed, and use `inspect_params: true` in `common.rs` when only some fields of a method are experimental.

ops.html: Client->server request payloads (*Params)
ops.src: ### Client->server request payloads (`*Params`)

ops.html: • Every optional field must be annotated with #[ts(optional = nullable)]. Do not use #[ts(optional = nullable)] outside client->server request payloads (*Params).
ops.src: - Every optional field must be annotated with `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`. Do not use `#[ts(optional = nullable)]` outside client->server request payloads (`*Params`).

ops.html: • Optional collection fields (for example Vec, HashMap) must use Option<...> + #[ts(optional = nullable)]. Do not use #[serde(default)] to model optional collections, and do not use skip_serializing_if on v2 payload fields.
ops.src: - Optional collection fields (for example `Vec`, `HashMap`) must use `Option<...>` + `#[ts(optional = nullable)]`. Do not use `#[serde(default)]` to model optional collections, and do not use `skip_serializing_if` on v2 payload fields.

ops.html: • When you want omission to mean false for boolean fields, use #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::​ops::​Not::​not")] pub field: bool over Option<bool>.
ops.src: - When you want omission to mean `false` for boolean fields, use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")] pub field: bool` over `Option<bool>`.

ops.html: • For new list methods, implement cursor pagination by default: request fields pub cursor: Option<String> and pub limit: Option<u32>, response fields pub data: Vec<...> and pub next_cursor: Option<String>.
ops.src:
- For new list methods, implement cursor pagination by default:
  request fields `pub cursor: Option<String>` and `pub limit: Option<u32>`,
  response fields `pub data: Vec<...>` and `pub next_cursor: Option<String>`.

ops.html: Development Workflow
ops.src: ### Development Workflow

ops.html: • Regenerate schema fixtures when API shapes change: just write-​app-​server-​schema (and just write-​app-​server-​schema --experimental when experimental API fixtures are affected).
ops.src:
- Regenerate schema fixtures when API shapes change:
  `just write-app-server-schema`
  (and `just write-app-server-schema --experimental` when experimental API fixtures are affected).

ops.html: • Validate with just test -p codex-​app-​server-​protocol.
ops.src: - Validate with `just test -p codex-app-server-protocol`.

ops.html: • Avoid boilerplate tests that only assert experimental field markers for individual request fields in common.rs; rely on schema generation/tests and behavioral coverage instead.
ops.src:
- Avoid boilerplate tests that only assert experimental field markers for individual
  request fields in `common.rs`; rely on schema generation/tests and behavioral coverage instead.
